precepts.text: Haman the Agagite sought to molest Mordecai and his people because of the two eunuchs, the assassins he hired to take the Persian throne from inside.
precepts.point: Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite: Agag was the Amalekite king of 1 Samuel 15, so Haman descended from the Edomites Saul failed to finish, and when he learned Mordecai was of Saul's line he sought to kill them all. From the womb to the tomb, this is war.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
“After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite”. Ahasuerus is Artaxerxes. Haman was the enemy in the book of Esther, the one who sought to kill all the Jews out of existence. And he is called the Agagite: in 1 Samuel 15, Agag was the king of the Amalekites, an Edomite king. Haman was a descendant of the survivors when King Saul went in and slaughtered them.

The Apocrypha tells the same man's story: “Howbeit Aman the son of Amadathus the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king.” When you read Esther, Haman hired two assassins to kill the king and take over the throne. The Greeks infiltrated the Persian Empire and tried to conquer it from the inside.

And when Haman found out that Mordecai was of the same line as King Saul, he said, that's Saul's line, kill them all; they tried to kill us off. They were going to go to war with them from generation to generation. We will never get along, from the womb to the tomb. This is war.

precepts.text: The canonical book records the same two chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, who sought to lay hands on the king, whom Mardocheus exposed through Esther, and who were both hanged on a tree.
precepts.point: This is the same account found in Esther chapter 2, where Mardocheus sat in the king's gate, uncovered the plot of the two chamberlains, and told it through Esther the queen. The king examined the two eunuchs, and after they confessed, they were strangled.

note.label: Esther 12: Mardocheus Uncovers the Plot and Aman's Hatred

precepts.why:
Mardocheus “took his rest in the court with Gabatha and Tharra, the two eunuchs of the king, and keepers of the palace.” He “heard their devices, and searched out their purposes, and learned that they were about to lay hands upon Artexerxes the king; and so he certified the king of them.” The king examined the two eunuchs, “and after that they had confessed it, they were strangled.”

This is the same account found in the canonical book. “In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.” Gabatha and Tharra are Bigthan and Teresh, the keepers of the palace who kept the door. The thing “was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai’s name.” He told it through Esther the queen, and the king was certified of it in his name.

“And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.” The king examined them, it was found out, and the two died for it. The Apocrypha and the canonical book are telling one story from two sides.

precepts.text: The canonical book promotes the same Aman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, setting his seat above all the princes.
precepts.point: The teaching traces who Aman was. He is the same Aman promoted in the canonical book, an Agagite, and the Agagites descend from Agag king of the Amalekites, and Amalek descends from Esau. This is the lineage that has warred against Israel throughout history and has always been unsuccessful, for the Most High delivered his people.

note.label: Esther 12: Mardocheus Uncovers the Plot and Aman's Hatred

precepts.why:
“Aman the son of Amadathus the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king.” When Mardocheus told on the eunuchs and had them put to death, Aman was upset, and he set himself to destroy not Mardocheus only but all the Israelites.

The canonical book shows where that great honour came from: “After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that were with him.” Amadathus is Hammedatha; it is the same Aman, the same Agagite, raised to the seat above all the princes.

Tracing him is the point. An Agagite descends from Agag king of the Amalekites, and Amalek descends from Esau. That is the lineage that has warred against Israel throughout history, and it has always been unsuccessful, for the Most High delivered his people.

note.label: Esther 12: Mardocheus Uncovers the Plot and Aman's Hatred

precepts.why:
Aman was in great honour with the king, but he was not one of the king's own people. The king's second letter says so: “Aman, a Macedonian, the son of Amadatha, being indeed a stranger from the Persian blood, and far distant from our goodness, and as a stranger received of us”. He was a Macedonian, a stranger from the Persian blood, received among the Persians and lifted up by them.

So the man who sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs was a stranger in the kingdom, an Agagite of the stock of Agag the Amalekite, of Esau, not a Persian. The honour he held was given him by a people he did not belong to, and he turned it against Israel.

note.label: Esther 12: Mardocheus Uncovers the Plot and Aman's Hatred

precepts.why:
Aman is called “the Agagite”, and Agag is a name with a history. Saul “took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.” Agag was king of the Amalekites; the Agagites descend from him, and that is the stock Aman comes from.

So when Aman sought to molest Mardocheus and his people, it was an Amalekite rising against Israel again. That line warred against Israel throughout history and was always unsuccessful, for the Most High delivered his people.

note.label: Esther 12: Mardocheus Uncovers the Plot and Aman's Hatred

precepts.why:
The line goes one step further back. “Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek”. Amalek was born to Eliphaz, Esau's son, so Amalek descends from Esau, who is Edom. The Amalekites come from Amalek, Agag was their king, and Aman the Agagite comes from Agag.

That is who was in great honour with the king and sought to molest Mardocheus and his people: a son of Esau. This is the lineage that has warred against Israel throughout history, and it has always been unsuccessful, because the Most High delivered his people.

points: The king made a record of these things, and Mardocheus also wrote of them. The king commanded him to serve in the court and rewarded him for it.
The canonical account in Esther chapter 2 did not mention the reward at that point, but as the account continues in chapter 3 and on you see how Mardocheus was honored for saving the king's life.
